newsitem.title: FINLAND: One-off items in M-Serla warning-analysts.
newsitem.headline: One-off items in M-Serla warning-analysts.

text.p: One-off factors and company-specific items as well as weak paper and pulp markets are behind a profit warning on Tuesday from Finnish forestry firm Metsa-Serla Oy, analysts said.
The company said it expected to make a loss in May-December, but a profit for full-year 1996.
Analysts expecting to downgrade forecasts pointed out this meant subtracting earnings from Metsa-Serla's 318 million markka first-tertial profit before extraordinaries.
"It's probably more than just problems in the market," said Dennis Christie at Kleinwort Benson in London.

Metsa-Serla cited a stronger than expected fall in pulp, and particularly paper, prices; but it also mentioned development projects and investments including restructuring at its recent German acquisition MD Papier, and starting a new paper mill.
Christie said these looked likely to have played a role, adding "it's not a good time to be starting up a new machine."
"I think most people will have to revise their forecasts down quite dramatically," he said.
Nine analysts polled by Reuters in June had pointed to a mean full-year profit around 800 million markka for Metsa-Serla, but the range then was already very wide at 130-1,106 million markka.
Anna-Maija Pirskanen at Merita Securities, said she would lower her 1996 forecast for Metsa-Serla, but not for other forestry groups.
"We have such a negative view at forestries in general, that we don't need to revise forecasts for other companies," she said, adding Merita has an underweight recommendation on forestries.
But although she saw one-off factors mainly behind Metsa-Serla's warning, she said it also underlined reason for caution in the forestry sector.
"This is mainly due to one-off factors, but we cannot deny that capacity ratios and paper prices have also declined," she said. "It seems that the recovery will be somewhat delayed."
Paper delivery times are quite long at six to eight weeks, so any future price increases cannot have any major effect on Metsa-Serla's profit for the rest of the year, Pirskanen noted.
"In that respect, the prospects have weakened," she said.
Jukka Huuskonen, analyst at Arctos Securities, also said the Metsa-Serla warning would not affect his forecasts or recommendations for other companies.
"It will affect my 1996 forecast for Metsa-Serla. There were quite a lot of one-off costs as they said themselves," he said.
